newsitem.title: ROMANIA: WESTERN COMPANIES BID FOR ROMANIA STEEL MAKER.
newsitem.headline: WESTERN COMPANIES BID FOR ROMANIA STEEL MAKER.

text.p: Romania's main privatisation agency said on Wednesday four western companies had bid for a 51 percent stake in a local stainless steel maker, the most modern such plant in central and eastern Europe.
"The State Ownership Fund (FPS) will look into the four bids for Otelinox and will announce the winner of the pre- selection by end-June," FPS official Luiza Sarpe said.
The winner or winners, expected to be announced on June 27, would then start negotiations with the FPS, she added.
The FPS is the majority stockholder of Otelinox, Romania's sole stainless steel maker based in Tirgoviste, 83 km (51 miles) north-east of Bucharest.
Sarpe said bids had been entered by Ugine, which belongs to France's Usinor Sacilor, by Samsung Deutschland GmbH and Italy's Stainless Steel International Spa and Finven Spa.
She said details of the bids remained confidential, but she said none of them had been up to FPS's asking level.
Sources close to the FPS said the price for the package of around 2.8 million shares on sale was around $15 per share.
Bid selection criteria include the size of the stake to be purchased, the price offered for that stake, further investment plans and environmental protection targets.

Local Intermob securities, which is preparing Otelinox's listing on the Bucharest stock exchange early next month, said the company had a share capital of around 141 billion lei. Otelinox now trades on the over-the-counter market.

Intermob manager Adrian Alexe said Otelinox had a net profit of 7.5 billion lei last year, up from 4.5 billion in 1995 and a loss of 4.6 billion lei in 1994. He said Otelinox's 1996 turnover had been some 41 billion lei up on 1995 at 92.4 billion. ($=7,205 lei)
